sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuyo* from B1 Unit 5. It means "whose" and joins the owner to the thing owned. It agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner, and no article goes before it. It is a good tool for describing places: Copán, *cuyas* stelae are famous, and the gulf, *cuyas* coasts belong to three countries.

sections.title: Cuyo agrees with the thing owned
rows: un rey cuyo nombre aparece en la escalinata
a king whose name appears on the stairway
una ciudad cuya historia está escrita en piedra
a city whose history is written in stone
la escalinata, cuyos escalones llevan glifos
the stairway, whose steps carry glyphs
el golfo, cuyas costas pertenecen a tres países
the gulf, whose coasts belong to three countries

items.spanish: Copán es una ciudad maya cuyas estelas fueron talladas en piedra volcánica.
items.english: Copán is a Maya city whose stelae were carved in volcanic stone.

items.spanish: La escalinata, cuyos escalones llevan más de dos mil glifos, cuenta la historia de la dinastía.
items.english: The stairway, whose steps carry more than two thousand glyphs, tells the history of the dynasty.

items.spanish: El golfo de Fonseca, cuyas aguas son compartidas, tiene manglares en sus orillas.
items.english: The Gulf of Fonseca, whose waters are shared, has mangroves on its shores.

items.spanish: Conocimos a una arqueóloga cuyo trabajo ayuda a leer los glifos.
items.english: We met an archaeologist whose work helps to read the glyphs.

sections.content: Do not put *que* before the possessive: not *una ciudad que sus estelas…*, but *una ciudad cuyas estelas…*. And no article: not *el cuyo*.
